distr continuous, bounded¶

Families on a bounded interval or a circle: proportions, bounded shapes and directions. Each page documents one family: the parameters, the support, how to evaluate the density and the distribution function, how to draw samples, and, for the families that have one, the object form and the maximum-likelihood fit.

The Surface¶

Family

What it is

Anglit

The anglit distribution: a cosine-shaped density on a symmetric interval, the distribution of the arcsine of a random square root.

Arcsin

The arcsine distribution: a U-shaped density on the unit interval that piles up at both ends.

Beta

The beta distribution: a flexible family on a bounded interval, the standard model of proportions and probabilities.

Bradford

The Bradford distribution: a density that decreases over the unit interval, with a single shape parameter.

Cosine

The cosine (raised cosine) distribution: a smooth, bounded, bell-shaped density on a symmetric interval.

HalfCosine

The half-cosine distribution: a single half-wave of a cosine as a density on a symmetric interval.

NormalTrunc

The truncated normal distribution: a normal distribution restricted to an interval.

Quadratic

The quadratic (parabolic, Epanechnikov) distribution: an inverted parabola as a density on a symmetric interval.

Semicircle

The semicircle (Wigner) distribution: a density in the shape of a half-circle, the limit law of the eigenvalues of large random symmetric matrices.

Triangular

The triangular distribution: a density that rises linearly to a mode and falls linearly, specified by its minimum, mode and maximum.

UShape

The U-shaped (symmetric arcsine) distribution: a density that is smallest at the centre and unbounded at both ends of a symmetric interval.

Uniform

The uniform distribution: every value in an interval is equally likely.

VonMises

The von Mises distribution: the circular analogue of the normal distribution, for angles.
